 Presented by Hot Topics From Titans HC Robert Saleh's Zoom Call on Monday
 Nov 16, 2026 at 09:33 AM Jim Wyatt Senior Writer/Editor
 Copied! 
 NASHVILLE – Titans coach Robert Saleh conducted a zoom conference call with reporters on Monday, one day after the team's 40-23 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars.
 The Titans return to action on Sunday at the Dallas Cowboys.
 Here's a look at some of the hot topics from today's call:
 -The most interesting part of Monday's call centered on quarterback Cam Ward, when Saleh said the team made a decision a few weeks ago, before the Browns game, to "shift our philosophy with how we wanted to approach offense and put more in his plate with regard to being a general at the line of scrimmage ... and having him be a field general." Saleh said they're now seeing "a young man who is getting comfortable with the offense, very comfortable with the verbiage." Saleh said Ward's footwork has improved, he's going through his progressions faster and "he's doing a really nice job playing quarterback." Saleh noted there are still things Ward needs to clean up, but he said he's improving. Ward has thrown at least two touchdowns passes in back-to-back weeks, and he had his first career 300-yard game against the Bengals in Week 8. "We made a shift philosophically with how we were going to approach this thing, and he's doing a really nice job taking command of it."
 So, why the shift?
 "To be fair to Cam, we've said from the beginning we were going to give him every opportunity to prove that he is a franchise quarterback of the Tennessee Titans," Saleh said of Ward, who has completion percentages of 64.5, 65.0 and 71.8 in the last three contests. "So, philosophically, the change was: How are we going to evaluate whether or not is he capable of being our franchise quarterback if we don't give him the opportunity to prove it? And I think over the last three weeks he has done that. Or, at least is doing it."
 -Saleh said the team will "hopefully" get receiver Carnell Tate, linebacker Anthony Hill Jr. and linebacker Cody Barton back for the Cowboys game.
 -Saleh said the team is hopeful to get guard Fernando Carmona, who was placed on Injured Reserve back in September, back at practice this week.
 -Saleh said the team is still evaluating the injuries from Sunday's game, which include Wan'Dale Robinson (ankle) and safety Tony Adams (concussion).
 -Speaking on the defensive struggles, Saleh said, "it's going to come down to play-making opportunities," especially on third down. Saleh mentioned several instances on Sunday when the Titans were in position to make plays, and they didn't make them. "Our guys are in position to make plays," Saleh said. "We just have to make plays."
 -Saleh said linebacker Cedric Gray, who had a team-high nine tackles and an interception, did a really nice job in Sunday's game, while also complimenting fellow linebacker Dorian Mausi, who handled the green dot for most of the game and was credited with seven stops.
 -Saleh said he made the decision to play Alontae Taylor over Marcus Harris at nickel on Sunday. Taylor played 61 defensive snaps vs the Jaguars, while Harris only played on special teams. "Alontae brings a different type of game," Saleh said. "Marcus is doing a really nice job, don't get me wrong. … We are not down on Marcus. … Alontae played at an All-Pro level at the nickel position (with the Saints) and yes, we tried to play him at corner, and we found that it is better to just let the man throw his fastball. We are working through some of the kinks here at nickel, but overall we have two really good options at that position."
 -Saleh said the team "has to do a better job of getting him involved" when asked about receiver Calvin Ridley, who only played four snaps and didn't have a catch on Sunday.
